translations.answer: M3imic can share one policy across robot-joint, SMPL-X, and five-end-effector references, but sparse end-effector commands trade full-body fidelity for robustness; each modality requires separate accuracy, success, and hardware-failure acceptance.
translations.applicability.assumptions.0: Paired robot, SMPL-X, and end-effector references are temporally aligned.
translations.applicability.assumptions.1: Deployment uses the reported G1 observation and action contracts.
translations.applicability.simulators.0: Isaac Lab stack reported by the official project.
translations.confidence_rationale: Training and unseen-motion tables plus official code support a shared controller and a modality trade-off; hardware reliability statistics remain incomplete.
translations.evidence.0.note: Defines three reference encoders and quantifies modality-dependent accuracy and success.
translations.evidence.0.title: M3imic: Learning a Versatile Whole-Body Controller for Multimodal Motion Mimicking
translations.title: Does sharing one controller across three motion inputs make their capabilities equivalent?
